title: The Photoelectric Effect
text: The photoelectric effect is the emission of electrons from a material when electromagnetic radiation, such as light, shines on it. Albert Einstein explained this phenomenon in 1905 by proposing that light consists of discrete packets of energy called photons, each with energy proportional to the frequency of the radiation. This was the first clear evidence for the quantization of electromagnetic radiation and earned Einstein the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921. The photoelectric effect is the basis for photovoltaic cells used in solar panels, which convert light directly into electricity. The minimum frequency of light needed to eject electrons from a surface is called the threshold frequency, which is characteristic of the material.
